exposure: Infant GBS colonization type (CC17 vs non-CC17)
outcome: De novo infant colonization by CC17 GBS
cohort: The study enrolled 890 mother-baby pairs in France who were positive for GBS colonization at antenatal screening or at delivery.
finding: The study found that infant colonization by CC17 GBS is strongly associated with simultaneous maternal colonization of the vagina and breast milk, and there is a higher risk for de novo CC17 colonization at 60 days post-delivery, suggesting enhanced post-delivery mother-to-infant transmission.
